messages.author: 4b63675507b4aa11
messages.subject: Multilevel spatial model
parts:
Dear All,

I am running a spatial (CAR) model on a data structure that has two conceptual levels: counties (cid) nested within states (sid). I want to include a spatial random effect at the county-level and a non-spatial random effect at the state-level. Here is what my formula looks like:

form <- out ~ 1 + f(cid, model = "bym", graph = "nb.adj") + f(sid, model = "iid")

Does this make sense?

Thanks.

Best,
Shige

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Multilevel spatial model
parts:
Hi

seems fine. just be aware of possible confounding with weak priors.

Best
H

messages.author: 4b63675507b4aa11
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Multilevel spatial model
parts:
Many thanks!

I'd like to continue with this example:
> form <- out ~ 1 + f(cid, model = "bym", graph = "nb.adj") + f(sid, model = "iid")

Now I want to improve that model by:

1. Changing it from "bym" to "bym2";
2. Using PC priors for both random effects.

Following Riebler et al. (2016), the "bym2" part of the model can be specified as:

> f(cid, model = "bym2", graph = "nb.adj", scale.model = TRUE,
    hyper = list(
      phi = list(
        prior = "pc",
        param = c(0.5, 2/3),
        initial = -3),
      prec = list(
        prior = "pc.prec",
        param = c(0.2/0/31, 0.01),
        initial = 5)))

Or simply:

> f(cid, model = "bym2", graph = "nb.adj", scale.model = TRUE)

Right? What about the "iid" part of the model? Does the following

> f(sid, model = "iid",
    hyper = list(
      prec = list(
        prior = "pc.prec",
        param = c(0.3/0.31, 0.01))))

make sense (p. 9-10 of Simpson et al., 2017)? Or should I calculate U based on the data at hand, as demonstrated in this example(http://www.maths.bath.ac.uk/~jjf23/inla/multilevel.html)?

Many thanks.

Best,
Shige
